note: The desk's fair values for EGX stocks, against the rest of the EGX. Figures are rebuilt by fetch_fairvalue.py; `judgement` (normalised earnings, brokers' fair values and the desk's note per stock) is written by the run and kept.

stocks.name: Madinet Masr for Housing & Development
stocks.note: The cheapest developer on earnings (4.9 times against about 8 for the group) and priced at its book value. The catch: developers book profit when homes are handed over, so a heavy delivery year flatters earnings, and the analysts' figure (EGP 9.70) sits far below the other two estimates.

stocks.name: Export Development Bank of Egypt
stocks.note: First-half profit rose 47% to EGP 3.9bn, yet it trades on 3.7 times earnings against 4.8 for banks. It is a small, thinly traded bank, and its 3.23-for-10 bonus issue adds shares, not value.

stocks.name: Orascom Development Egypt (S.A.E)
stocks.note: All three estimates land between EGP 12.50 and 16.50. First-half net income rose 4.5% to EGP 3.17bn and real estate sales 30% (EnterpriseAM).

stocks.name: Misr Fertilizers Production Company MOPCO
stocks.note: The three estimates agree within about 12%. The risk is gas: rationing cut output this year, and the desk's open view has fertilizer stocks under pressure through November.

stocks.name: Egypt Aluminum
stocks.note: Cheap on earnings made at a high aluminium price, so the gap narrows if the metal falls. The state is weighing a stake sale and the real free float is near 3%.

stocks.name: Palm Hills Development Co.
stocks.note: Al Ahly Pharos puts it at EGP 21.40 on existing assets alone; the desk's figure is lower because it weighs today's earnings and book value as much as brokers' forecasts.

stocks.name: Commercial International Bank - Egypt (CIB) S.A.E.
stocks.note: Measured against other banks only: a third-quarter profit down 17% (last year's quarter had a one-off provision release) still leaves it on 4.9 times earnings with a 32% return on equity.

stocks.name: Telecom Egypt
stocks.note: Valued on last year's consolidated profit (EGP 11.93 a share), because Mubasher's lower figure looks to cover the parent company only. Close to fair on all three estimates.

stocks.name: EFG Holding S.A.E.
stocks.note: Priced at its book value with all three estimates within 10% of each other; the return on equity (11%) is what holds it back.

stocks.name: Raya Holding for Financial Investments SAE
Fawry For Banking Technology And Electronic Payment
stocks.note: The widest disagreement on the list: 19 times earnings is dear against its peers, while brokers who value its growth (Al Ahly Pharos: EGP 28.60) see more than 50% upside. Treat the figure as unsettled.

stocks.name: Talaat Moustafa Group Holding
stocks.note: The estimates disagree: analysts' targets are well above the price on the land bank and the EGP 11 trillion state deal, while today's earnings and book value put it slightly below.

stocks.name: Cleopatra Hospital Company
stocks.note: A growth stock on a growth multiple (32 times earnings). The model gives growth only a 25% allowance, so it will always look dear here; analysts' EGP 14 target is close to the price.

stocks.name: MM Group for Industry & International Trade
Alexandria Containers & Goods
stocks.note: A fine business at a full price: 15 times earnings and 12 times book. Naeem's EGP 33.60 target is where it trades now.

stocks.name: Juhayna Food Industries
stocks.note: The desk's projection (EGP 27–28 by end of January) rests on results momentum. On value alone it is dear: 16 times earnings against about 12 for consumer stocks. The two can both hold for a while; they cannot both be right for long.

stocks.name: El Sewedy Electric Company
stocks.note: The dearest of the large companies: 16 times earnings against about 11 for industrials, and all three estimates sit below the price. The market is paying for the order book abroad.

stocks.name: Abou Kir Fertilizers & Chemical Industries Co.
stocks.note: Same gas risk as MOPCO, with results to September already in the figures. The dividend yield is above 11%.

stocks.name: Suez Canal Bank SAE
stocks.action: Moved +53.2% in one session, beyond the EGX's 20% limit: most likely a bonus issue or split. Check that the earnings and book value per share are on the new share count before trusting the fair value.
stocks.note: The one large bank the model finds dear: 8.3 times earnings against 4.8 for the others, with no analyst coverage to argue otherwise.

stocks.name: Tenth of Ramadan Pharmaceutical Industries & Diagnostic-Rameda
stocks.note: As with Cleopatra: 33 times earnings for fast profit growth. Dear unless the growth lasts.

stocks.name: e-finance for Digital and Financial Investments S.A.E.
stocks.note: On last year's consolidated profit over today's share count it trades on 44 times earnings; Mubasher's per-share figure, which looks to predate the bonus shares, gives 25. Analysts' targets sit near the price. The estimates are far apart, so confidence is low.

stocks.name: Mohandes Insurance Co.
stocks.note: Thirty times earnings for an insurer earning 14% on equity. Thinly researched; no analyst estimate.

stocks.name: Beltone Holding
stocks.note: An EGP 10.5bn capital increase multiplied the share count while quarterly profit stayed flat (EGP 695m against 702m a year earlier), leaving it on 39 times earnings with a 3% return on equity.

notRated.name: Orascom Construction Plc
notRated.why: its figures predate the OCI merger, which adds 97.2 million shares for assets valued at $1.35bn; not comparable until the merged accounts are out

notRated.name: Bonyan for Development and Trade
notRated.why: its reported profit (EGP 2.0bn in 2025) is more than twice its rental revenue (EGP 752m), so most of it is not rent and a P/E does not describe it
